purpose: Define bounded representation candidates and MultiSWAP cost gates before any production-like prototype.

source_bound_baseline: theta-space finite-water-content bins are fixed by discretization
about 150-200 bins over the full theta_r to theta_e range are reported for accurate infiltration-front profiles
front positions and falling-slug/groundwater-front regimes evolve dynamically
forward-Euler timestep guidance is of order 10 s for infiltration, 100 s for falling slugs and up to 500 s for groundwater-front dynamics
nonuniform bin distributions are explicitly suggested by the paper as a possible way to reduce bin count

candidate_A_fixed_or_semifixed_theta_bin.description: Keep a fixed bounded theta-bin layout per hydraulic material/template. Dynamic state is stored in fixed-index arrays for front/occupancy quantities; no dynamic allocation is allowed during a trial.
candidate_A_fixed_or_semifixed_theta_bin.native_lineage: closest to the published FWC discretization
advantages: constitutive K(theta) and psi(theta) values can be immutable shared data
deterministic indexing and transaction-safe trial buffers
risks: 150-200 uniform bins may be too much persistent state/work for very large MultiSWAP batches
falling-slug multiplicity is not yet proven representable by a fixed finite number of coordinates per bin
explicit internal timestep count may dominate runtime under infiltration
depth-profile views require reconstruction/projection from theta-domain geometry
candidate_A_fixed_or_semifixed_theta_bin.promising_variant: offline nonuniform theta bins chosen from hydraulic/solution-resolution criteria shared by a template, never validation-case-specific per column
candidate_A_fixed_or_semifixed_theta_bin.hard_gate: Any reduction in bins must be qualified against a high-resolution FWC reference and FullRichards; performance policy may not silently coarsen physical representation.

candidate_B_dynamic_front_object_pool.description: Store only active infiltration, slug and groundwater-front intervals as dynamic objects rather than dense per-bin dynamic arrays.
candidate_B_dynamic_front_object_pool.native_lineage: derived representation, not the published fixed-bin implementation
advantages: could reduce state when only a small subset of theta space is active
may avoid work on empty bins
risks: object count can depend on forcing history
front creation/merge/sort operations introduce branch divergence
unbounded pool growth would violate compact predictable MultiSWAP state
hard capping or merging objects can alter physics unless separately qualified
less suitable for contiguous SoA/vector execution
candidate_B_dynamic_front_object_pool.hard_gate: Reject as production representation unless a source- or algorithm-derived finite maximum object count is proven for arbitrary admitted forcing, with conservative deterministic merge rules.

candidate_C_fixed_bins_with_bounded_fron.description: Hybrid research candidate: fixed/nonuniform theta bins plus a fixed predeclared number of front/slug coordinate slots per bin or per column, all stored in SoA form.
advantages: preserves bounded allocation and batch layout while allowing more than one disconnected interval if required
transactional trial state can be copied or checkpointed predictably
risks: maximum slot count is currently unknown
overflow policy cannot discard or merge water silently
large worst-case slot counts can erase the expected memory advantage
candidate_C_fixed_bins_with_bounded_fron.hard_gate: Official-code audit or a complete event-topology proof must establish the required maximum slot count before this representation can be admitted.

must_report: internal ODE steps per external interval
maximum not just mean internal steps
runtime_cost_model_to_measure.bounded_cost_requirement: All production-admitted configurations require explicit finite maxima or fail-closed retry/rejection rules; no unbounded event or front growth.

reason: It is closest to the source method and best aligned with fixed-layout MultiSWAP batching. Dynamic object compression should not be introduced before the source implementation and event topology are understood.
